Messages.Author: wesile
Messages.Body:
> Karen Suadela, 7, POT CEL pre obf, Brujah, 5, [KoT]
> Camarilla Prince of Houston: Gehenna cards do not affect Karen while she is a prince. She gets +1 stealth on undirected actions.
>
> New Inquisition, The, Event, 1 Gehenna card, R , [G]
> Gehenna. Do not replace until a titled vampire goes to torpor. Requires at least one other Gehenna card in play. During each Methuselah`s untap phase, he or she may choose a ready vampire controlled by his or her prey. That vampire takes 1 unpreventable damage. Any titled vampire may call a referendum to burn this card as a +1 stealth political action.
>
The question is...does karen take damage from New Inquisiton???

I am thinking that she is immune... but lets hear it from the Judge...

Thanks

Messages.Author: Kiddo
Messages.Body:
Why would she take damage? As long as she's a Prince, she is unaffected by any Gehena cards, which New Inquisition is.

Why do you think there are any doubts about that?

Messages.Author: wesile
Messages.Body:
Just checking... since the effect is triggered by other Methuselah I decided to check...

Its always nasty to be playing a card and hearing from someone something like:

->There is a ruling regarding that card that says this and that... you cannot do that.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> wesile wrote:
> Just checking... since the effect is triggered by other Methuselah I decided to check...
>
Who is triggering the card is irrelevant. The source of damage is the card (not the Methuselah). Since it's a Gehenna, Karen is immune to it.
[/quote]

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
It's that general ruling principle that won't let you call Parity Shift if you have the most pool, won't let you call Reckless Agitation if there is only one other player than yourself, etc. It's the "Can't use an effect/take an action if there are no valid targets" concept. PB and LSJ have frequently dragged it out.

So the question is... can you use New Inquisition (a Gehenna card) to target Karen Suadela even if you know she is "immune" to Gehenna cards. Or in another sense: Is Immunity to a Card Type (e.g. Immune to Gehenna Cards) the same as "unable to be targeted by a card type" or "targeting this minion with that card type has no effect"?

Retired Baron of Sydney, Australia, 418

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
@Juggernaut : what you describe is very different from "you can't take actions/use effects that would have no results", no ? AFAIK, you can use, eg, Horsehoe on Ponti, he won't die but it's not illegal

> Non-existant user wrote:
> You can choose Ponticulus as a target for the Talbot Chainsaw damage. I don't see why this one should be any different.
>
Well, there is a difference : Ponticulus is immune to the damage done by the Talbot effect, but not to the effect. Karen is immune to the whole package.
